001package io.github.ai4ci.config.setup;
002
003import java.io.Serializable;
004
005import org.davidmoten.hilbert.HilbertCurve;
006import org.davidmoten.hilbert.SmallHilbertCurve;
007import org.immutables.value.Value;
008
009import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonIgnore;
010import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonDeserialize;
011import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonSerialize;
012
013import io.github.ai4ci.abm.Abstraction;
014
015/**
016 * Configuration used during model setup and initialisation.
017 *
018 * <p>
019 * Main purpose: encapsulate the parameters and strategies required to create
020 * agents and construct their contact network at the start of a simulation.
021 * Features include:
022 * <ul>
023 * <li>the number of initial imports used to seed an outbreak;</li>
024 * <li>a pluggable network generation strategy via
025 * {@link NetworkConfiguration};</li>
026 * <li>a pluggable demographic strategy via
027 * {@link DemographicConfiguration};</li>
028 * <li>utility methods for spatial placement such as {@link #hilbertBits()} and
029 * {@link #getHilbertCoords(Integer)}.</li>
030 * </ul>
031 *
032 * <p>
033 * Downstream uses: instances are consulted by model builders and initialisers
034 * during setup. Typical consumers include
035 * {@link io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.DefaultPersonInitialiser} and
036 * {@link io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.AbstractModelBuilder}. Implementations
037 * are commonly generated by Immutables (see
038 * {@link ImmutableSetupConfiguration}).
039 *
040 * @author Rob Challen
041 */
042@Value.Immutable
043@JsonSerialize(as = ImmutableSetupConfiguration.class)
044@JsonDeserialize(as = ImmutableSetupConfiguration.class)
045public interface SetupConfiguration extends Abstraction.Named,
046                Abstraction.Described, Abstraction.Replica, Serializable {
047
048        /**
049         * Default setup configuration used in examples and tests.
050         */
051        ImmutableSetupConfiguration DEFAULT = ImmutableSetupConfiguration.builder()
052                .setName("default")
053                .setInitialImports(30)
054                .setDemographics(LocationAwareDemography.DEFAULT)
055                .setNetwork(ErdosReyniConfiguration.DEFAULT)
056                .build();
057
058        /**
059         * Demographic configuration.
060         *
061         * <p>
062         * This selects the demographic strategy used when creating persons and when
063         * computing pairwise relationship strengths. Common implementations include:
064         * <ul>
065         * <li>{@link UnstratifiedDemography} — draws strengths from a single
066         * distribution;</li>
067         * <li>{@link AgeStratifiedDemography} — samples ages and adjusts contact
068         * odds by age difference;</li>
069         * <li>{@link LocationAwareDemography} — supplies spatial placement and
070         * proximity based modifiers.</li>
071         * </ul>
072         *
073         * <p>
074         * Demographic implementations are responsible for providing
075         * {@link DemographicConfiguration#createPersonStub} used during setup and
076         * {@link DemographicConfiguration#getRelationshipStrength} used when
077         * composing contact probabilities. If you need richer per‑person data (for
078         * example loading census CSVs) provide a custom Demographic implementation
079         * and register it via Jackson polymorphism.
080         *
081         * @return the demographic configuration used during person creation and
082         *         baselining
083         */
084        DemographicConfiguration getDemographics();
085
086        /**
087         * For sequentially created networks such as Watts‑Strogatz the geographical
088         * location can be decided by the ring position. This will tend to create a
089         * network that has geographical location correlating to network topology.
090         *
091         * <p>
092         * The returned coordinates are normalised to the unit square [0,1]x[0,1] and
093         * are suitable for assigning {@code locationX/locationY} on
094         * {@link io.github.ai4ci.abm.PersonDemographic} during setup. The method
095         * uses a Hilbert curve with bits chosen to provide adequate resolution for
096         * the configured network size.
097         *
098         * @param id the ring position (for example the sequential node index)
099         * @return an X‑Y geographical location (range 0 to 1)
100         */
101        @JsonIgnore
102        default double[] getHilbertCoords(Integer id) {
103                double size = this.getNetwork()
104                        .getNetworkSize();
105                var hilbert = this.hilbertBits();
106                var tmp = hilbert
107                        .point((long) (id / size * Math.pow(2, hilbert.bits() * 2)));
108                return new double[] { (tmp[0]) / Math.pow(2, hilbert.bits()),
109                                (tmp[1]) / Math.pow(2, hilbert.bits()), };
110        }
111
112        /**
113         * Number of initial cases to seed the outbreak with.
114         *
115         * <p>
116         * Used by {@link io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.DefaultPersonInitialiser} to
117         * compute a simple per‑person importation probability during initialisation.
118         * The value represents a coarse seeding strategy; for more sophisticated
119         * seeding (geographically localised or stratified by demographic) supply a
120         * custom initialiser in a composed
121         * {@link io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.AbstractModelBuilder}.
122         *
123         * @return the number of initial imports to seed
124         */
125        Integer getInitialImports();
126
127        /**
128         * Should the R0 value be calibrated to this specific individual network
129         * (true) or against a standard Erdos-Reyni network (false). If comparing
130         * networks against each other this should be set to false so that the
131         * effects of network topology on transmission is not lost through
132         * re-calibration of transmission probability.
133         * 
134         * @return true if R0 is normalised to the network topology, false otherwise.
135         */
136        @Value.Default
137        default boolean isCalibrateR0ToNetwork() { return true; }
138
139        /**
140         * Network generation configuration.
141         *
142         * <p>
143         * The returned {@link NetworkConfiguration} defines which graph model is
144         * used to construct the social network during the setup stage. The project
145         * provides a few common implementations:
146         * <ul>
147         * <li>{@link ErdosReyniConfiguration} — classical G(n,p) random graph;</li>
148         * <li>{@link WattsStrogatzConfiguration} — small‑world rewired lattice;</li>
149         * <li>{@link BarabasiAlbertConfiguration} — preferential attachment / scale
150         * free.</li>
151         * </ul>
152         *
153         * <p>
154         * Builders call {@link NetworkConfiguration#generateGraph} passing an empty
155         * JGraphT {@code SimpleGraph<Person,DefaultEdge>} to populate nodes and
156         * edges. To add a new topology implement a new configuration type and
157         * register it with the Jackson polymorphic mapping used by the config
158         * loader.
159         *
160         * @return the network configuration used for agent placement and contact
161         *         construction
162         */
163        NetworkConfiguration getNetwork();
164
165        /**
166         * Utility method to compute a Hilbert curve with bits chosen to provide
167         * adequate resolution for the configured network size. This is used by
168         * {@link #getHilbertCoords(Integer)} to compute spatial coordinates for
169         * agents based on their ring position. The returned curve is 2‑dimensional
170         * and has bits chosen such that the total number of points on the curve is
171         * at least the network size, ensuring a unique coordinate for each agent.
172         *
173         * @return a SmallHilbertCurve instance with bits set for the configured
174         *         network size
175         */
176        @JsonIgnore
177        default SmallHilbertCurve hilbertBits() {
178                double size = this.getNetwork()
179                        .getNetworkSize();
180                var bits = (int) Math.ceil(0.5 * Math.log(size) / Math.log(2));
181                return HilbertCurve.small()
182                        .bits(bits)
183                        .dimensions(2);
184        }
185
186}
